part5_reasoning: RetainedAcquisitionStoreV2 is a complete, already-implemented, already-factory-wired, already-tested production-capable bounded writer. It requires NO new code to activate -- only a configuration change (flip RETAINED_ACQUISITION_OBSERVATIONS_ENABLED to '0' and RETAINED_ACQUISITION_V2_SHADOW_ENABLED to '1' in the creator_funding_worker supervisor block) and a restart of that single process. This is not a partial integration and not proof-only tooling being mistaken for readiness -- the exact same factory function (_configured_retained_store) that the live process calls today already returns RetainedAcquisitionStoreV2 when the flag is set, proven by both existing and newly-added tests calling that function directly.

part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.daily_payload_byte_counter: YES -- self._payload_bytes, incremented only on successful budgeted writes
part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.hard_refusal_after_cap: YES -- _is_within_budget() / _write_budgeted() return False once self._payload_bytes + payload_bytes would exceed daily_payload_cap_bytes
part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.cap_minimum_clamp: the constructor enforces max(1_000_000, requested_cap) -- a cap below 1MB is silently raised to 1MB, not honored literally (discovered and documented via test_daily_cap_has_a_1mb_minimum_clamp)
part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.metadata_only_fallback_if_qualified: YES -- on budget refusal, retain() stores the condensed hot payload (_build_v2_hot_payload) instead of failing the write entirely; verified the full-payload-only fields (response_data, response_text, raw_body_base64, request_payload) are absent from the hot fallback while identity/replay fields remain present
part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.hot_store_ceiling: governed by the same daily_payload_cap_bytes -- there is no SEPARATE ceiling for hot-payload volume; hot payloads are always written regardless of cap (they are the fallback, not a second budgeted tier)
part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.archive_before_retire_semantics: NOT PRESENT in RetainedAcquisitionStoreV2 itself -- this class only decides full-vs-hot payload shape per observation; archive/retire of the legacy DB is a SEPARATE, not-yet-designed concern explicitly out of scope for this milestone (Problem B)
part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.disk_reserve_floor: YES -- shutil.disk_usage(self.path.parent).free < 10 * GIB_BYTES refuses ANY write (full or the write attempt itself) once free space drops below 10 GiB; this matches the exact floor this session has independently been enforcing at the B2N milestone-gate level
part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.fail_open_or_closed_relative_to_acquisit: FAIL-OPEN for acquisition itself: RetainingTransactionAcquisition.request_once() wraps store.retain()/record_outcome() in a try/except that only journals a degraded-accounting event on failure -- it never raises into or blocks the underlying acquisition response. FAIL-CLOSED for the retention WRITE specifically: _write_budgeted() cleanly refuses (returns False, does not raise) rather than writing an oversized payload; the caller then substitutes the hot payload, which is always written regardless.
part7_hard_growth_control_enforcement.no_missing_enforcement_invented: the above is a direct, literal restatement of what the code does, verified with 9 passing tests this milestone; nothing was assumed or exaggerated

fields_confirmed_present_in_hot_fallback: artifact_digest, artifact_size_bytes, artifact_compressed_bytes, content_type (artifact linkage -- the raw response body itself lives in the separate ArtifactStore, referenced by digest, not duplicated inline)
request_payload_sha256, response_headers_sha256 (request/response identity as digests, not full bulk payload)
metadata subset: launch, purpose, provider, method, request_type, timestamp (provider/method identity, timestamps/boundaries)
fields_confirmed_absent_from_hot_fallbac: raw_body_base64 (bulk, but recoverable via artifact_digest -> ArtifactStore)
part8_evidence_semantics_preserved.conclusion: No field required for deterministic replay, migration lineage, correlation identity, provider/method identity, request/response identity, or artifact linkage is removed. Bulk payload bytes are the ONLY thing dropped in the hot fallback, and only when the daily cap is already exhausted or disk is low -- and even then, the raw bytes remain recoverable via the artifact digest into the separate, already-existing ArtifactStore, not destroyed.

preserve all bounded artifacts (the new bounded DB and its artifact store) -- do not delete them on rollback
record the failure in the handoff/audit trail rather than silently reverting
